L2: ENROLLING SOON
L3: # A clinical study for dogs with hemangiosarcoma
L4: 
L5: If your dog has recently been diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, our clinical study at the University of Illinois Veterinary Hospital in Urbana may be an option, and there is no cost to take part. The study is testing FAM-010, a new investigational chemotherapy designed to be gentler on the heart. Your dog may be eligible if they recently had their spleen removed or have surgery scheduled.
L6: 
L7: [Button: Contact the study team]
L8: 【1†Image: A calm dog resting its head on a bed while a person gently pets it.】
L9: ## What is hemangiosarcoma?
L10: 
L11: Hemangiosarcoma is an aggressive cancer that starts in the blood vessels, most often in the spleen. It often shows few signs until a tumor bleeds, so many dogs are diagnosed suddenly, sometimes in an emergency.
L12: 
L13: Treatment usually starts with surgery to remove the spleen, followed by chemotherapy. Even with both, the cancer often comes back, and there is still no FDA-approved treatment for hemangiosarcoma in dogs.
L14: ## How is FAM-010 different?
L15: 
L16: Doxorubicin is the current standard chemotherapy for dogs with hemangiosarcoma after surgery. But it can also reach and damage healthy tissues, especially the heart. This limits the total amount of chemotherapy a dog can receive.
L17: 
L18: FAM-010 is a new form of doxorubicin, designed to carry more of the medicine to the cancer and less of it to the heart. We hope this will let dogs receive more of the treatment they need, more safely.
L19: ## What will this study tell us?
L20: 
L21: This first study will find the right dose of FAM-010 for dogs: the highest dose they can receive without side effects becoming too much. Every dog in the study receives FAM-010, given as a short infusion every three weeks at the University of Illinois, and the study team monitors each dog closely throughout.
L22: 
L23: FAM-010 is investigational and not approved by FDA for dogs. This study is designed to establish the dose and understand its side effects.
L24: 
L25: STUDY ELIGIBILITY
L26: ## Could this study be an option for your dog?
L27: 
L28: If the following apply to your dog, we encourage you to contact us. Our study team will review your dog’s medical history and test results to confirm eligibility.
L29: 
L30:   * ### Diagnosis
L31: 
L32: A pathology report has confirmed hemangiosarcoma of the spleen, or you are waiting for the result.
L33: 
L34:   * ### Recent spleen surgery
L35: 
L36: Your dog has had their spleen removed or has surgery scheduled.
L37: 
L38:   * ### Timing
L39: You are able to travel to the study site in Urbana Illinois within 21 days after surgery.
L40: 
L41:   * ### Previous treatment
L42: 
L43: Your dog has not received chemotherapy, radiation or another investigational drug.
L44: 
L45:   * ### Travel to Urbana, Illinois
L46: 
L47: You could bring your dog to Urbana for regular study visits.
L48: 
L49:   * ### Breeding
L50: 
L51: Your dog is not intended for breeding.
L52:

L2: For veterinarians
L3: # Help shape the medicines your patients need next.
L4: 
L5: Familiar is building a new generation of medicines for companion animals, informed by the veterinarians who care for them. Whether you're interested in clinical trials, want to share an unmet need, or simply want to connect with our team, we'd love to hear from you.
L6: 
L7: 【1†Get involved】
L8: 
L9: 【2†Image: A veterinarian in teal scrubs with a stethoscope holding a small tan puppy and a tabby kitten in a bright exam room.】
L10: 
L11: OUR APPROACH
L12: ## Translated from human medicine.
L13: 
L14: Many diseases in dogs and cats share underlying biology with human disease. Familiar starts with drug candidates whose targets and mechanisms are already understood in people, then does the translational work required to determine whether they can become veterinary medicines.
L15: Before a program advances, we confirm target biology, pharmacokinetics, dosing, and clinical feasibility in the animals we intend to treat. Where we can, we pursue medicines designed to change the course of the disease, not only manage its signs.
L16: 
L17: 【3†Image: A smiling veterinarian in blue scrubs holding a happy golden retriever in a bright exam room.】
L18: 
L19: FROM PIPELINE TO PRACTICE
L20: ## Designed to work in everyday veterinary practice.
L21: 
L22: 01
L23: 
L24: ### Oral-dose small molecules
L25: 
L26: Where the biology allows, we favor oral small molecules: medicines you can prescribe in a telehealth consult and have delivered directly to your client’s door.
L27: 
L28: 02
L29: 
L30: ### Scalable from the start
L31: 
L32: We assess manufacturability and scalability early, so promising programs can reach more patients.
L33: 
L34: 03
L35: ### Developed with a companion test
L36: 
L37: Wherever possible, we pair a program with a companion test, so patient selection doesn't depend on a referral.
L38: 
L39: 04
L40: 
L41: ### Shaped by practicing veterinarians
L42: 
L43: We develop our programs with input from veterinarians in real-world clinical practice, including general practitioners.
L44: 
L45: 【4†Explore our pipeline →】
L46: 
L47: SCIENTIFIC ADVISORY BOARD
L48: ## Developed with veterinarians
L49: 
L50: Familiar's Scientific Advisory Board includes practicing veterinarians who bring the realities of day-to-day clinical care into our development process, helping shape program selection, indication strategy, and clinical-trial design.
L51: 
L52: 【5†Meet our full scientific advisory board →】

L2: Company news Press release·October 21, 2026
L3: # Familiar Therapeutics Launches with $5 Million Seed to Close the Gap Between Human and Veterinary Medicine
L4: 
L5: In its first five months, Familiar has built 13 programs for dogs and cats, signed several pharma partnerships, filed a provisional patent and opened two drug development files with FDA CVM.
L6: 
L7: Programs span oncology, neurology, cardiology, respiratory disease, and immunology, with the company's first clinical study set to open at the University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital this fall
L8: 【1†Image: Familiar Therapeutics Launches with $5 Million Seed to Close the Gap Between Human and Veterinary Medicine】
L9: REDWOOD CITY, Calif.: Familiar Therapeutics launched today with $5 million in seed funding to bring the advances of modern human medicine to dogs and cats. The round was led by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures and BreakTHRU, a syndicate of animal-health industry leaders and veterinarians, with participation from angel investors, including a co-founder of fintech company Robinhood and a founding member of OpenAI and Y Combinator.
L10: Over the past two decades, a new generation of medicines has changed the outlook for people with chronic and life-threatening diseases. Dogs and cats develop many of the same diseases as people, often driven by the same underlying biology, yet very little of that medical progress has reached them. Fewer than 10 new drugs are approved by the FDA each year for companion animals, compared with more than 50 for people.
L11: For many serious conditions, veterinarians still rely on human medicines used off-label, without dosing or safety data for the species. Much of the science needed to change this exists, but adapting a drug for animals takes its own clinical studies, manufacturing work and FDA review. Without a dedicated path for that work, promising medicines rarely make it across to dogs and cats.
L12: Familiar was built to close that gap. Because each program starts with years of human research behind it, Familiar aims to bring disease-modifying medicines to pets significantly faster than the seven to ten years a new animal drug typically takes. The company works with pharmaceutical and biotech partners on each program, licensing the veterinary rights to their drugs and leading the clinical development and manufacturing work needed for FDA approval in dogs and cats.
L13: In the five months since its founding, Familiar built a pipeline of four lead programs and nine earlier-stage programs for dogs and cats, signed multiple partnership and licensing agreements with biopharmaceutical companies, opened two investigational new animal drug (INAD) files with the FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine and filed one provisional patent. The seed funding will move its lead programs into clinical studies and advance the rest of its pipeline.

L2: # They're family. Their medicine should be familiar.
L3: 
L4: Familiar translates proven human medicines into novel therapeutics for the animals who share our lives, designed to reach every pet, through every veterinary clinic.
L5: 
L6: 【1†See our pipeline】【2†Contact us】
L7: 
L8: The opportunity
L9: ## Our pets get the same diseases we do. They deserve the same breakthroughs.
L10: 
L11: Dogs and cats develop many of the same cancers, immune disorders, and other serious diseases that affect people, but the medicines available to treat them haven’t kept pace. For families and veterinarians, that means facing devastating diagnoses with too few options.
L12: 
L13: We believe pets deserve medicines that can change the course of disease. Familiar exists to help make that possible.
L14: 
L15: Our approach
L16: ## Built on human science.
L17: Developed for pets.
L18: 
L19: Familiar takes proven human drug candidates with validated targets and established safety data, and translates them into novel therapeutics for companion animals.
L20: 
L21: We partner with the pharma and biotech companies that developed these medicines. From there, we take on the veterinary development work: animal-specific research, clinical studies and the path to FDA approval.
L22: ### And because the biology is shared, the science flows both ways.
L23: 
L24: Dogs and cats develop these diseases naturally, making companion animal clinical programs a powerful source of early efficacy signal for human drug development.
L25: 
L26: Enrolling soon
L27: 
L28: FAM-010 CLINICAL STUDY
L29: ## Advancing a new treatment for dogs with hemangiosarcoma.
L30: 
L31: We are launching a clinical study to evaluate FAM-010 in dogs recently diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma. FAM-010 is a new form of doxorubicin, designed to deliver more medicine to tumors while reducing exposure to healthy tissue, so dogs can receive more of the treatment they need.
L32: 
L33: 【3†See if your dog qualifies】[Button: Refer a patient →]
L34: 
L35: FAM-010 is an investigational drug and is not approved by FDA.

L39:     Dogs recently diagnosed with hemangiosarcoma of the spleen

L42:     University of Illinois College of Veterinary Medicine, Urbana, Illinois
L43: 
L44: Study stage
L45:     Pilot study, the first study in dogs, to set the dose and look for early signs the drug helps
L46: ## FAM-010 is one of 13 programs bringing advances in human medicines to pets.
